entities.summary: Wratislav I, Count of Fürstenberg was a prominent diplomat and officer in Spanish and Austrian service. Born in unknown year, he died on July 10, 1631. His significance lies in his role as President of the Imperial Court Council, which marked a turning point in the history of the Holy Roman Empire. The appointment of Wratislav I to this position in 1627 underscored the growing influence of the Habsburgs in European politics. Wratislav I's diplomatic career was marked by his service as a mediator in conflicts between the Holy Roman Empire and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. He played a key role in negotiating the Treaty of Deułchów in 1627, which brought an end to the Polish-Swedish War. The treaty's provisions, which included the recognition of Polish sovereignty, marked a significant shift in the balance of power in Eastern Europe. Wratislav I's legacy extends beyond his diplomatic achievements, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Catholic Church. His contributions to the cultural and religious life of the Holy Roman Empire have been recognized by historians as an important aspect of his historical significance. The Wratislav I statue in the Fürstenberg Castle complex in Lüneburg, Germany, serves as a lasting tribute to his memory. The Wratislav I family crest features a proud eagle, symbolizing his commitment to the Habsburg dynasty. The coat of arms, which includes a silver eagle on a red background, has been preserved and displayed in the castle since the 17th century.

entities.summary:
Wratislav von Fürstenberg (1584-1631) was a prominent figure in the early modern era, serving as an officer in Spanish and Austrian service, a diplomat, and President of the Imperial Court Council. Born in Prague, he played a significant role in European politics during the Thirty Years' War.

As a diplomat, Wratislav von Fürstenberg worked closely with notable figures such as Cardinal Richelieu and Emperor Ferdinand II, influencing the course of European history. His involvement in the war led to significant territorial changes, with the Treaty of Westphalia in 1648 shaping the modern European map.

Despite his influence, Wratislav von Fürstenberg's legacy remains somewhat overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, but his contributions to European politics and diplomacy are undeniable.

In the end, Wratislav von Fürstenberg's impact on world history can be seen in the intricate web of alliances and rivalries that defined the early modern era.
